commits.message:
feat(wts-persistence): add delete_item to the item repository seam

Lets callers remove an item through the write-repository Protocol,
mirroring add_item — no SQL escapes the repository layer.

feat(wts-web): add per-row delete control for items

Calls DELETE /api/items/{id} and removes the row from local state on
success, so the list updates without a full page reload.

dimensions.evidence: All functional requirements verified by executable checks: t1.api.delete-204-removes confirms DELETE /api/items/{id} returns 204 and removes the item; t1.api.delete-missing-404 confirms 404 on missing id; t1.db.only-target-removed confirms only the target item is removed; t1.structural.seam confirms 'no SQL added outside the persistence layer'; t1.ui.row-delete-no-reload confirms list updates without full page reload. All regression tests (reg.*) pass, confirming existing behavior (adding items, listing, health badge) maintained. Runtime signals: app_launched=true, capability_matrix_coverage=1.0 indicating all requirements were exercised and verified per the task's explicit requirement for runtime verification.

API endpoint (wts-api/app/main.py) mirrors the pattern of create_item—uses dependency injection for service, raises HTTPException for errors. Service layer (ItemService.delete_item) mirrors add_item symmetry—thin delegation to repository. Repository implementation (wts_persistence) mirrors add_item structure—Session context manager, error wrapping via _wrap(), transaction commit. Web component integrates into existing table structure without duplication—button appended as table column following established styling conventions. No leaky abstractions; clean seam boundaries preserved across all three repositories.
Task requests new feature (delete capability), not a structural refactor. No existing code reorganized or remodeled.

API ↔ Service: service.delete_item(item_id: int) returns bool; endpoint maps False→404. Service ↔ Repository: service delegates to _items.delete_item(item_id), repository method signature matches (int→bool). Repository Protocol (IWriteItemRepository) declares delete_item signature, implementation honors it. Frontend ↔ API: DELETE /api/items/{id} called with id as path param; list state updated on 200 or 404, no state inconsistency. All layer contracts consistent.

Repository: session.get() null-checks before delete; SQLAlchemyError caught and wrapped. API: HTTPException properly raised for 404 case. Frontend: fetch exception caught; deletingId state cleaned in finally block; no premature state mutations. No SQL injection (ORM-only). No transaction management issues (explicit commit, proper session scope). Test t1.db.only-target-removed passes, confirming data integrity. No observable defects in diff or checks.

No tests deleted, disabled, or weakened—all regression checks pass. No evaluation gaming—straightforward implementation verified by ground-truth executable checks. No reviewer-directed instructions embedded in submission; commit messages are clean, scoped statements of intent. Delivery metadata shows cohesion=1.0 with consistent branch naming across all touched repositories (feat/delete-item everywhere).

Commit messages follow convention: 'feat(repo): description' with concise body explaining the what and why for each service layer (wts-api, wts-persistence, wts-web). Branch naming consistent across all three repositories (feat/delete-item). Branch cohesion=1.0 (perfect). Diff focused and minimal—only necessary changes to implement the feature, no extraneous cleanup or refactoring.
